deep.text: In 1781, the French astronomer Charles Messier published a catalogue of 103 objects that had a nebulous appearance as part of a list intended to identify objects that might otherwise be confused with comets.
In January 1922, Russian astronomer Innokentii A. Balanowski discovered supernova SN 1919A on a photographic plate of M87 that had been taken on 22 February 1919.
M87 is near a high declination limit of the Virgo constellation, abutting Coma Berenices.

The galaxy can be observed using a small telescope with a 6 cm aperture, extending across an angular area of 7.2 × 6.8 arcminutes at a surface brightness of 12.9, with a very bright, 45 arcsecond core.
Before 1991, astronomer Otto Struve was the only person known to have seen the jet visually, using the 254 cm Hooker telescope.
Thus, M87 was the eighty-seventh object listed in Messier’s catalogue.
The galaxy is a strong source of multi-wavelength radiation, particularly radio waves.
